children: , the retail and digital-marketplace giant, faced a bipartisan push for Federal Trade Commission scrutiny of its Sparky AI shopping assistant after Senators Tammy Baldwin and Rick Scott asked the agency to investigate how the tool handles Made in USA products. Walmart shares traded at $107.18 Friday.

The senators' request follows research alleging that Sparky can identify American-made merchandise and potentially detect questionable country-of-origin claims, yet does not consistently surface those products or flag potentially misleading listings. Reuters reported that Walmart had not commented on the senators' request, while the FTC had also not responded. Importantly, this remains a request for investigation rather than an FTC finding against Walmart.

That turns Sparky into more than a shopping feature. If AI recommendations increasingly depend on regulated product claims, Walmart may need tighter seller documentation, cleaner origin data and stronger escalation controls before those systems can scale without creating additional compliance work. The valuation picture is hardly stretched, though: the chart shows Walmart at $107.18 versus a GF Value of $104.09, leaving the shares only 2.97% above GF Value. That modest premium suggests investors are paying close to GuruFocus' estimated fair-value level even as AI-driven marketplace oversight becomes another operational issue to watch.

title: Walmart Gains as Sparky Draws a Made-in-USA Probe Request
